text:
By David Moye ,
5 hours ago
Vice President JD Vance attempted to mock a Democratic senator and veteran after she pressed Secretary of State Marco Rubio over whether the U.S. is at war with Venezuela.
During a Senate Foreign Relations Committee hearing on Wednesday, Rubio insisted the U.S. isn‚Äôt at war with the South American nation, which prompted Sen. Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.) to ask him if he would advise the president ‚Äúto rescind his invocation of the wartime Alien Enemies Act?‚Äù

‚ÄúOf course not,‚Äù Rubio responded. ‚ÄúWhen it comes to narco-trafficking gangs and criminal gangs, there‚Äôs no doubt about the fact that we‚Äôre confronting them in a war-like setting.‚Äù
The heated exchange apparently caught Vance‚Äôs eyes, and he saw a chance to troll Duckworth ‚Äî a Purple Heart recipient and former Army helicopter pilot who lost her legs and partial use of her right arm during the Iraq War in 2004 ‚Äî by comparing her to (checks notes) Forrest Gump.
Watching Tammy Duckworth obsessively interrupt Marco Rubio during this hearing is like watching Forest Gump argue with Isaac Newton.
Vance might have thought he scored points with that post, but Duckworth countered with a strong, sharp retort that favorably compared the actions of Tom Hanks‚Äô iconic film character with those of the president himself.
‚ÄúForrest Gump ran toward danger in Vietnam. Your boss ran to his podiatrist crying bone spurs,‚Äù she pointed out, before adding that ‚Äúpetty insults at the expense of people with disabilities won‚Äôt change the fact that you‚Äôre risking troops‚Äô lives to boost Chevron‚Äôs stock price.‚Äù
She added that her job as a senator is to ‚Äúhold you accountable.‚Äù

Vance never did engage with Duckworth‚Äôs skillful verbal parry, instead responding to the original post with unabashed words of biblical praise for Rubio.
‚ÄúThank God we have a Secretary of State who knows his facts AND has the patience of Job. Great job, @SecRubio,‚Äù he posted.
